Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the background into a basketball court
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is there visible evidence that the background has begun changing toward a basketball court, even though completion is not established by this check?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows discernible progress toward replacing the background with a basketball court, including basketball-related scene changes or partial court cues. Fail if there is no visible progress toward that requested background change. Unknown if progress cannot be distinguished from the original or assessed reliably. This is a progress judgment, not a completion judgment; a complete court background may also pass.
node.binding: Assess only progress toward the requested background replacement. Do not use this check to decide whether the background is complete; unrelated edits do not count as progress.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image replaces the kitchen background with visible basketball-related scene elements, including a hoop, basketballs, and court markings, showing clear progress toward the requested background change.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is truncated and less specific than the executable criterion, which requires a recognizable court background—not merely basketball-related objects. Repair the binding so it consistently evaluates the whole replacement background, including whether the visible playing surface and court markings or equivalent court context make it read as a basketball court; do not let a hoop or balls alone establish completion. Preserve the separate partial-progress path: basketball-themed replacement elements can show progress when the court itself is not established, while unrelated edits do not count. Here s1’s stated failure and s2’s progress support partial under the supplied criteria, so the yes reference label alone is not evidence to relabel this as complete. The traces are valid and queried, with no transport or dependency failure; investigate the disagreement as a possible criterion/binding or visual-evidence ambiguity rather than treating confidence or the reference as atomic ground truth.
